newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on short covering, firm cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on short covering, firm cash.

text.p: Short covering amid signals the market was oversold boosted CBOT wheat futures to a higher close as did firm soft red winter cash wheat markets and commercial bull spreading, traders said.

"There's still four million (bushels) left open in the September and cash SRW wheat is very strong," said Steve Bruc e of E.D. and F. Man International. "Plus Continental did 600,000 Dec/Mar out of the chute today and that set the tone."
Traders said the wheat market had been hit hard recently and was in an oversold mode technically.

Continental Grain spread 600,000 bushels of December/March and also was the key stopper of 295,000 bushels of the total 300,000 bushels posted Monday for delivery on the expired September contract, traders said.
Wheat weather got mixed reviews with some saying the rain will delay seedings and others saying the moisture will help boost growth prospects of the 1997 U.S. winter wheat crop.
Iowa Grain and Prudential Securities each bought 1.5 million bushels of December, traders said. Cargill Inc sold two million December, they said.
Wheat futures closed 1-1/2 to six cents per bushel higher, with December up 5-1/2 cents at $4.26-1/2 a bushel.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 11,000, up from 10,745 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Continental Grain bought 300 December $5.00 calls at one cent, the traders said.
Options volume was estimated at 2,500, up from 2,453 Friday.
